intended_object: The component at level n of the natural isomorphism between the residue diagram n ↦ ℤ/n and the power-quotient diagram n ↦ G/G^n of a procyclic profinite group G. It is the isomorphism ℤ/n ≅ G/G^n that sends 1 to the class of a chosen topological generator g. This comes from the docstring and from its only use, in `residuePowerQuotientNatIso`.
explanation:
This is a packaging step for a proof. It takes the library's own equivalence `powerImage_zmodContinuousMulEquiv` (ℤ/n ≃ G/G^n, sending 1 to the class of g), removes the universe lift `ULift`, notes that both stages carry the discrete topology so the map is continuous, and turns the result into an isomorphism in `ProfiniteGrp`. Its only job is to supply the components that `NatIso.ofComponents` needs in `residuePowerQuotientNatIso`.

The actual mathematical content, the isomorphism ℤ/n ≅ G/G^n determined by the generator, lives in `powerImage_zmodContinuousMulEquiv`. This declaration adds only category-theory and universe bookkeeping. The hypotheses (G procyclic, g a topological generator, the index of G^n equal to n) are exactly the ones the construction needs, and the simp lemmas below the definition confirm that it computes the intended map. So it is correct as an auxiliary device, but it is not a standalone mathematical notion to judge for faithfulness or generality. Mathlib has no counterpart.
